title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
authors: DeepSeek-AI (about 200 authors, listed alphabetically by first name within each role in Appendix A)

code.title: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3
code.note: weights (FP8, with a BF16 conversion script) and inference demo code; code under MIT, weights under the DeepSeek Model License, which allows commercial use (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path)

takeaway: 671B/37B-active MoE matching GPT-4o-class models via MLA, aux-loss-free routing, MTP, and FP8/DualPipe co-design for 2.788M H800 hours (~$5.6M marginal compute).
verdict: Believe the engineering and the bill as the paper defines it: one final run, and the GPU hours agree with a FLOPs count at the same utilisation Llama 3 reported. Treat the MTP and auxiliary-loss-free wins as real but small, single-run and not quite like for like, and the benchmark tables as the authors' own harness.

headline.k: the whole official run: pre-training, context extension, post-training
headline.d: $5.576M at an assumed $2 an hour; excludes research and ablations

headline.k: parameters active per token: 8 of 256 routed experts plus 1 shared, in 58 of 61 layers
FP8 against BF16 training, relative, at 16B and 230B scale for about 1T tokens

resources.n: the clearest derivation of MLA from MHA, MQA and GQA, including the decoupled RoPE trick.
context on what the $5.576M figure does and does not cover, and why the release landed the way it did.
an independent sanity check that the claimed GPU hours are plausible for a 37B-active MoE on 14.8T tokens; the Check the bill tab redoes it with the paper's own numbers.
maps the paper's equations to the released code.
the open-source week that released the kernels this report describes: DeepGEMM (FP8 GEMM), DeepEP (all-to-all), DualPipe, EPLB (redundant experts), with profiling data.

kb.n: 2025: the RL-based reasoning successor built on V3-Base, and the distillation source for V3's own reasoning SFT data.

2024: an earlier open MoE design, 8 large experts and top-2.

2019: the tensor parallelism V3 manages without.
2024: the dense 405B baseline V3 overtakes with 37B active parameters; its utilisation figures anchor the Check the bill tab.
2022: basis of V3's self-rewarding feedback for open-ended RL.

kb.t: Bounding the memory bottlenecks of large MoE training
kb.n: later work on where MoE training memory goes.
